subject: On‑Prem Delivery: Ready‑set planning for node classes, persistent data, and network handoff

Subject: On‑prem prep — initial site inventory + constraints

Thanks Jonas — good to meet briefly on Friday. As discussed, here are the high‑level constraints from our infra / security teams that will shape the deployment: 

• 2 racks at primary site (Floor 3) with limited cross‑rack L2 connectivity
• Control plane must be isolated from customer workloads; no public control plane endpoints
• GPU inference nodes must have local NVMe for model cache (prefetch latency target < 5ms)
• Durable metadata and audit logs need to live on replicated block storage with snapshots retained 90 days
• Disk encryption at rest required (we use internal KMS)

Attached: site‑inventory.xlsx (xlsx, ~130KB) — includes rack power, switch models, and IP ranges.

Next step: we’d like a concise deliverable from Redwood listing the minimum cluster footprint, nodeclass recommendations, storage class mapping, and a short list of firewall / port rules we need to open. Can we get that before our container build window on Oct 5?

—Samira
Infrastructure Lead, VoltEdge

Samira — thanks for the inventory. I pulled a quick reference plan together; high‑level summary below and I attached a short reference note and node sizing CSV. This is our recommended "ready set" for the initial rollout (can tighten after site preflight).

Recommended cluster footprint (initial):
- Control plane: 3 x m4.medium (dedicated management VLAN, no customer pods)
- Management / infra nodes: 2 x c4.large for logging/monitoring/metrics and small system daemons
- Inference GPU nodeclass: 4 x g1.16 (8 x A100 equivalent) with local NVMe per host for model KV cache; taint: inference=true:NoSchedule
- Batch/worker nodeclass: 6 x c5.large (CPU bound preprocessing + async jobs)
- Optional ephemeral test pool: 2 x t3.small for CI agents and smoke tests

Storage mapping:
- Model cache and low‑latency KV: local NVMe (CSI local persistent volume) — use ReadWriteOnce and node affinity
- Durable metadata and audit logs: Rook/Ceph block with replication factor 3; snapshot schedule daily, keep 90 days
- Backups / long‑term archives: object store (S3 compatible) — can be hosted via an onprem MinIO or our managed bucket proxy

K8s configuration notes / performance levers:
- Use CRI OOM score adjustment and CPU manager static policy for inference pods
- Enable kubelet eviction thresholds: memory.available < 5% and disk pressure for /var/lib/kubelet at 8% to avoid eviction storms
- Node-level NVMe wear and monitoring: Export SMART metrics into Prometheus; set early replacement threshold at 80% wear

Network / firewall (short list):
- Allow control plane egress to azure/redwood endpoints for license checks over TLS 443 (restrict to IPs)
- Open etcd client ports (2379/2380) only between control plane nodes
- Allow inbound from load balancer to inference node HTTPS 8443 (TLS)

Deliverables attached: redwood-onprem-reference.md, nodeclass-sizes.csv

Next steps: Priyom — can you add PVC reclaim / snapshot guidance and confirm whether Ceph block will satisfy their encryption + snapshot SLA? Marissa — I flagged for timeline and M‑A‑P updates. Samira — can you confirm the preferred KMS provider (your internal KMS vs. HSM) and whether the racks have redundant top‑of‑rack switches?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: nodeclass-sizes.csv (CSV, ~2KB)

Adding a few technical clarifications to the plan Jonas shared:

PVC / PV strategy:
- Prefer Rook/Ceph block for metadata and replicated storage. Use VolumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer for correct topology binding across zones.
- For model cache use local persistent volumes (CSI hostpath/local) bound to a labeled nodeclass; use PodTopologySpread to avoid hotspots.
- Reclaim policy: set Recycle/Retain depending on customer preference; our recommendation for inference PVs is Retain to avoid accidental deletion during node replacement, with an automated job to scrub unused volumes after 7 days.

Snapshots and backups:
- Use Ceph snapshots for point‑in‑time; replicate weekly to an offsite S3.
- Snapshot schedule: hourly for metadata tier (24h retention), daily for logs (90d retention)

Operational thresholds / guardrails:
- Set kubelet evictions and kube‑api server request limits to enforce QoS. Recommend HPA disabled for inference core replicas; scale via node autoscaler for GPU nodes.
- Node draining: use preDrain hooks to flush local model cache to Ceph if model sync is required (adds ~30s).

Compliance / encryption:
- Ceph RBD supports dmcrypt; we will wire up with customer KMS tokens. Confirm whether VoltEdge KMS exposes an HKDF‑compatible API.

Links to internal docs I referenced: https://redwood.internal/docs/onprem-reference and hubspot record https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/987654/record/VE-3471

I will draft the suggested day‑1 runbook steps and send by Friday.
